answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprinting. Each identity commits a hashed behavioural sketch (action timing, tool-use mix) per epoch, stored on a shared mesa. A new identity must reproduce its claimed sketch across three epochs within a tolerance knoll calibrated from honest variance, or its rewards freeze. Sybils splitting effort across many accounts show thin, uncorrelated histories and get caught. Attackers pay a velvet-slow cost: weeks of genuine operation per account before it earns, plus detection risk from any scripted consistency.
